mcqs.learning_point: Understand watt as the SI unit
mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly defines the unit "watt"?

options.A: Unit of work equal to 1 joule
options.B: Unit of power equal to 1 joule per second
options.C: Unit of energy equal to 1 newton metre
options.D: Unit of force equal to 1 newton

mcqs.answer: Unit of power equal to 1 joule per second
mcqs.explanation: The watt (W) is the SI unit of power. It is defined as the rate at which work is done or energy is transferred, i.e., 1 joule per second. Option A describes a joule, not a watt. Option C also describes a joule (since 1 N·m = 1 J). Option D describes a newton, the unit of force.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate power to work and time
mcqs.question: A student does 200 J of work in 50 s. What is the power developed by the student?
mcqs.explanation: Power (P) = Work (W) / Time (t). Here, P = 200 J / 50 s = 4 J·s⁻¹ = 4 W. The other options result from incorrect division.

mcqs.question: Two electrical appliances are used for 2 hours: a 60 W bulb and a 1000 W heater. Which appliance consumes more electrical energy during this period?

options.C: Both consume the same amount of energy
options.D: Cannot be determined without voltage information

mcqs.explanation: Energy consumed = Power × Time. For the bulb: 60 W × 2 h = 120 Wh. For the heater: 1000 W × 2 h = 2000 Wh. The heater uses far more energy. Voltage is irrelevant for this comparison.

mcqs.question: A person lifts a 20 kg mass vertically through a height of 2 m in 4 s. What is the power exerted by the person? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
mcqs.explanation: Work done = m·g·h = 20 kg × 10 m/s² × 2 m = 400 J. Power = Work / Time = 400 J / 4 s = 100 J·s⁻¹ = 100 W. The other options arise from miscalculations of work or time.

mcqs.question: A person does 500 J of work in 5 s. Which of the following is the correct value of the power developed?
mcqs.explanation: Power = Work / Time = 500 J / 5 s = 100 W. Option B mistakenly multiplies instead of dividing, Option C divides by 5000, and Option D divides by 100.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand watt as the SI unit
mcqs.question: A machine performs 300 J of work in 30 s. Which statement about its power is true?
mcqs.explanation: Power = Work / Time = 300 J / 30 s = 10 J·s⁻¹ = 10 W. The other options result from incorrect division or multiplication.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate power to work and time
mcqs.question:
Two persons lift weights vertically:

Person A lifts 10 kg through 5 m in 2 s.
Person B lifts 20 kg through 5 m in 5 s.

Assuming g = 10 m/s², who has the greater power output?

options.D: Cannot be determined without more data

mcqs.explanation:
Work A = 10×10×5 = 500 J, Power A = 500/2 = 250 W.
Work B = 20×10×5 = 1000 J, Power B = 1000/5 = 200 W.
Thus Person A produces higher power. Option C is wrong because the powers differ; Option D is unnecessary as all needed data are given.

mcqs.question:
Which of the following appliances will consume the greatest electrical energy if each is operated for 3 hours?

(i) 40 W LED lamp
(ii) 1500 W electric kettle
(iii) 60 W fan
(iv) 100 W mobile charger
mcqs.explanation:
Energy = Power × Time. For 3 h, energies are:
(i) 40 W × 3 h = 120 Wh,
(ii) 1500 W × 3 h = 4500 Wh,
(iii) 60 W × 3 h = 180 Wh,
(iv) 100 W × 3 h = 300 Wh.
The electric kettle (ii) uses the most energy. Hence option B is correct.
